Utilizes a lightweight zero-shot depth model to generate dense depth maps for improved reconstruction.
insights: 创新点：提出基于高斯散布的SLAM系统
方法亮点：采用连续时间轨迹优化框架进行位姿估计
关键发现：零样本深度模型提高重建质量
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed Gaussian Splatting SLAM system
Method highlight: Pose estimation within a continuous-time trajectory optimization framework
Key finding: Zero-shot depth model improves reconstruction quality
abstract: This paper presents a photo-realistic LiDAR-Inertial-Camera Gaussian Splatting SLAM system that simultaneously addresses visual quality, geometric accuracy, and real-time performance. The proposed method performs robust and accurate pose estimation within a continuous-time trajectory optimization framework, while incrementally reconstructing a large-scale 3D Gaussian map using camera and LiDAR data, all in real time. The resulting map enables high-quality, real-time novel view rendering of both RGB images and depth maps. To effectively address under-reconstruction in regions not covered by the LiDAR, we employ a lightweight zero-shot depth model that synergistically combines RGB appearance cues with sparse LiDAR measurements to generate dense depth maps. The depth completion enables reliable Gaussian initialization in LiDAR-blind areas, significantly improving system applicability for sparse LiDAR sensors. To enhance geometric accuracy, we fully use sparse but precise LiDAR depths to supervise Gaussian map optimization and accelerate it with carefully designed CUDA-accelerated strategies. Furthermore, we explore how the incrementally reconstructed Gaussian map can improve the robustness of the odometry. By efficiently incorporating photometric constraints from the Gaussian map into the continuous-time factor graph optimization, we demonstrate improved tracking performance, especially under LiDAR degenerated scenarios. We also showcase downstream applications via extending our elaborate system, including video frame interpolation and fast 3D mesh production. To support rigorous evaluation, we collect a dedicated LiDAR-Inertial-Camera dataset featuring ground-truth poses, depth maps, and extrapolated trajectories for assessing out-of-sequence novel view synthesis in large-scale outdoor scenarios. Extensive experiments on both public and self-collected datasets demonstrate the superiority and versatility of our system across LiDAR sensors with varying sampling densities.

title: FoMo: A multi-season dataset for robot navigation in Forêt Montmorency
summary_zh: 构建FoMo数据集，包含多季节森林环境下的机器人导航数据，挑战现有里程计和SLAM流程。数据集包含超过64公里轨迹，多次重复部署，涵盖多种环境变化。
summary_en: Constructs the FoMo dataset, a multi-season dataset for robot navigation in a boreal forest, challenging existing odometry and SLAM pipelines. The dataset includes over 64 km of trajectories, repeated during 12 deployments throughout the year, covering various environmental changes.
insights: 创新点：构建多季节森林环境下的机器人导航数据集
方法亮点：挑战现有里程计和SLAM流程
关键发现：数据集包含多种环境变化
insights_en: Novelty: Constructed multi-season robot navigation dataset in a boreal forest
Method highlight: Challenges existing odometry and SLAM pipelines
Key finding: Dataset includes various environmental changes
abstract: The Forêt Montmorency (FoMo) dataset is a comprehensive multi-season data collection, recorded over the span of 1 year in a boreal forest. Featuring a unique combination of on- and off-pavement environments with significant environmental changes, the dataset challenges established odometry and SLAM pipelines. Some highlights of the data include the accumulation of snow exceeding 1 m, significant vegetation growth in front of sensors, and operations at the traction limits of the platform. In total, the FoMo dataset includes over 64 km of six diverse trajectories, repeated during 12 deployments throughout the year. The dataset features data from one rotating and one hybrid solid-state lidar, a Frequency Modulated Continuous Wave radar, full-HD images from a stereo camera and a wide lens monocular camera, as well as data from two IMUs. Ground Truth is calculated by post-processing three GNSS receivers mounted on the Uncrewed Ground Vehicle (UGV) and a static GNSS base station. Additional metadata, such as one measurement per minute from an on-site weather station, camera calibration intrinsics, and vehicle power consumption is available for all sequences. To highlight the relevance of the dataset, we performed a preliminary evaluation of the robustness of a lidar-inertial, radar-gyro, and a visual-inertial localization and mapping techniques to seasonal changes. We show that seasonal changes have serious effects on the localization capabilities of state-of-the-art methods. The dataset and development kit are available at https://fomo.norlab.ulaval.ca .

title: Fast Feature Field (F 3 ): A general predictive representation of events for robot perception
summary_zh: 开发基于事件相机的Fast Feature Field (F 3 )，通过预测未来事件来学习场景结构和运动信息。F 3 利用事件数据的稀疏性，并高效计算，适用于多种下游任务。
summary_en: Develops Fast Feature Field (F 3 ) for event-based cameras, learning scene structure and motion information by predicting future events. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and computes efficiently, suitable for a range of downstream tasks.
insights: 创新点：开发基于事件相机的Fast Feature Field (F 3 )
方法亮点：利用事件数据的稀疏性
关键发现：适用于多种下游任务
insights_en: Novelty: Developed Fast Feature Field (F 3 ) for event-based cameras
Method highlight: Exploits the sparsity of event data
Key finding: Suitable for a range of downstream tasks
abstract: This paper develops a mathematical argument and algorithms for building representations of data from event-based cameras that we call Fast Feature Field (F 3 ). We learned this representation by predicting future events from past events and show that it preserves scene structure and motion information. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and is robust to noise and variations in event rates. It can be computed efficiently using ideas from multiresolution hash encoding and deep sets, achieving 120 hertz at high-definition (HD) resolution and 440 hertz at video graphics array (VGA) resolution. F 3 represents events in a contiguous spatiotemporal volume as a multichannel image, enabling a range of downstream tasks. We obtained state-of-the-art performance on optical flow estimation, semantic segmentation, and monocular metric depth estimation, on data from three robotic platforms (a car, a quadruped robot, and a flying platform) and across different lighting conditions (daytime and nighttime), environments (indoors, outdoors, urban, and off-road), and dynamic vision sensors (resolutions and event rates). Our implementations can predict these tasks at 25 to 75 hertz at HD resolution.

title: MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing
summary_zh: MonoRace利用单目相机和IMU进行无人机竞速，无需外部运动跟踪系统。结合神经网络和无人机模型进行状态估计，实现冠军级无人机竞速。
summary_en: MonoRace uses a monocular camera and IMU for drone racing without external motion tracking. Combines neural network-based gate segmentation with a drone model for robust state estimation, achieving champion-level drone racing.
insights: 创新点：使用单目相机和IMU进行无人机竞速
方法亮点：结合神经网络和无人机模型进行状态估计
关键发现：实现冠军级无人机竞速
insights_en: Novelty: Monocular camera and IMU-based drone racing
Method highlight: Combines neural network and drone model for state estimation
Key finding: Achieves champion-level drone racing
abstract: Autonomous drone racing represents a major frontier in robotics research. It requires an artificial intelligence (AI) that can run onboard lightweight flying robots under tight resource and time constraints while pushing the physical system to its limits. The state of the art in this area consists of a system with a stereo camera and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) that beat human drone-racing champions in a controlled indoor environment. Here, we present MonoRace, an onboard drone-racing approach that generalizes to a competition environment without any external motion tracking system, using only a monocular rolling-shutter camera and an IMU. The approach features robust state estimation that combines neural network–based gate segmentation with a drone model. Moreover, it includes an offline optimization procedure that leverages the known geometry of gates to refine any state estimation parameter. This offline optimization is based purely on onboard flight data and is important for fine-tuning the extrinsic camera calibration parameters. Furthermore, the guidance and control are performed by a neural network that forgoes inner-loop controllers by directly sending motor commands. This small network runs on the flight controller at 500 hertz. The proposed approach won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition 2025, outperforming all competing autonomous drone race teams and three world champion human pilots in a direct knockout tournament. It reached speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour on the competition track and successfully coped with problems such as camera interference and IMU saturation.

AIRLoc: An IoU-Guided Adaptive Fusion Method for Floorplan-Based Visual Localization

title: A genetically encoded local learning rule enables physical learning in engineered bacteria
summary_zh: 开发遗传编码的局部学习规则，实现工程细菌中的物理学习。通过环境输入激活局部启动子，将信号转换为生长差异。
summary_en: Developed a genetically encoded local learning rule enabling physical learning in engineered bacteria. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, converting signals into differential growth.
insights: 创新点：提出遗传编码的局部学习规则实现物理学习
方法亮点：实现细菌中的物理学习，无需外部设备
关键发现：通过生长差异存储模拟权重
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed a genetically encoded local learning rule for physical learning
Method highlight: Achieved physical learning in bacteria without external devices
Key finding: Storing analog weights as differential growth to simulate learning
abstract: Abstract Training physical neural networks directly in matter remains difficult because most platforms do not store and update weights within the same physical substrate. Here we show that engineered Escherichia coli can implement a genetically encoded local learning rule acting on persistent biological memory. We introduce memregulons: bacterial memory elements in which coupled plasmids store an analogue weight as the relative abundance of P1 within the P1 + P2 plasmid pool. Environmental inputs activate local promoters, and a shared sublethal kanamycin signal converts promoter activity into differential growth that lowers the stored P1 fraction. Across single-strain trajectories, combined plate-reader and flow-cytometry measurements are consistent with activity- and variance-dependent weight change. At the single-cell level, repeated negative learning reshapes the stored weight distribution as it approaches the lower boundary. In mixed populations and co-cultures, one shared negative learning signal selectively rewrites active memregulons, enabling externally routed supervised tic-tac-toe lessons. We then generalise the architecture across orthogonal chemical inputs and combinatorial promoters, and combine measured co-culture updates with external game analysis and simulate negative pruning in nonlinear-classifier architectures. These results establish physical learning in living matter through local negative updates of genetically encoded analogue weights.

title: Energy-efficient precision weed elimination using a quadruped robot
summary_zh: 研究提出一种四足机器人高效除草方法。该方法协调任务，优化能量消耗。模型显示高效任务分配可节省能量。
summary_en: This study proposes an energy-efficient precision weed elimination method using a quadruped robot. The method coordinates tasks and optimizes energy consumption. The model indicates energy savings through efficient task allocation.
insights: 创新点：提出高效除草机器人方法
方法亮点：任务协调与能量优化
关键发现：高效任务分配节省能量
insights_en: Novelty: Proposed an energy-efficient weed elimination method using a quadruped robot
Method highlight: Task coordination and energy optimization
Key finding: Energy savings through efficient task allocation
abstract: In precision agriculture, an autonomous weed-removal robot (i.e., mobile manipulator) often faces a combination of challenges including large-scale navigation, repetitive coverage, and fine-grained intervention. These challenges give rise to a distinct energy-efficient long-horizon planning problem: coordinating ordered, repetitive, and heterogeneous tasks under domain-specific temporal and geometric constraints. In precision weeding, this problem is further characterized by (i) an observe-first-and-manipulate-later type temporal constraint and (ii) the potential for substantial energy savings through efficient task collocation. We formalize this challenge and propose a new problem: Repetitive and Clustered-Coupled Active Perception and Manipulation (RC-CAPM) problem for mobile manipulators. We model RC-CAPM as a stochastic renewal process and show, via the Renewal Reward Theorem, that the expected energy consumption per task cycle converges to a well-defined long-run average. We introduce a task-space partitioning method that enumerates all feasible task-multiplexing configurations and their associated probabilities under robot reachability constraints. We then derive a two-stage optimization framework and prove that its solution is optimal and equivalent to that of the original RC-CAPM problem. We evaluate the proposed approach in both simulation and on a physical mobile manipulator performing autonomous weeding. Across all evaluations, RC-CAPM consistently outperforms baseline planning strategies, yielding reductions in path length, number of stops, replanning events, and total energy consumption. In particular, the proposed method achieves an average energy reduction of 36.1% relative to the baseline.

title: MORPHIT: Flexible spherical approximation of robot morphology for representation-driven adaptation
summary_zh: MORPHIT框架允许机器人通过可调参数进行形态适应。实验表明，该框架提高适应性和效率。
summary_en: The MORPHIT framework allows robots to adapt their morphology with tunable parameters. Experiments show that this framework improves adaptability and efficiency.
insights: 创新点：提出MORPHIT框架，实现机器人形态适应。
方法亮点：基于梯度优化，实现参数可调。
关键发现：提高适应性和效率。
insights_en: Novelty: Introduces the MORPHIT framework for robot morphology adaptation.
Method highlight: Based on gradient optimization for tunable parameters.
Key finding: Improves adaptability and efficiency.
abstract: What if a robot could rethink its own morphological representation to better meet the demands of diverse tasks? Most robotic systems today treat their physical form as a fixed constraint rather than an adaptive resource, forcing the same rigid geometric representation to serve applications with vastly different computational and precision requirements. We introduce morphit , a novel spherical approximation framework that treats morphological representation as a tunable resource. morphit enables automatic task-driven morphological adaptation through gradient-based optimization with tunable parameters that provide explicit control over the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff. Unlike existing approaches that rely on either labor-intensive manual specification or inflexible computational methods optimized for visualization rather than robotics, morphit generates spherical approximations up to 100x faster than optimization-based methods while maintaining superior geometric fidelity. Quantitative evaluations demonstrate that morphit outperforms baseline approaches and achieves better mesh approximation with fewer spheres. Through seamless integration with existing robotics infrastructure, morphit enables enhanced capabilities in collision detection accuracy, contact-rich interaction simulation, and navigation through confined spaces. By dynamically adapting geometric representations to task requirements, robots can now exploit their physical embodiment as an active resource rather than an inflexible parameter, opening new frontiers for manipulation in environments where physical form must continuously balance precision with computational tractability.

title: Competing mechanisms toughen bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K
summary_zh: 研究20 K下bcc二元和中等熵合金的强化机制。实验表明，孪晶和ω相变提高强度。
summary_en: This study investigates the strengthening mechanisms of bcc binary and medium-entropy alloys at 20 K. Experiments show that twinning and ω-phase transformation enhance strength.
insights: 创新点：发现20 K下合金的强化机制。
方法亮点：评估孪晶和ω相变的影响。
关键发现：孪晶和ω相变提高强度。
insights_en: Novelty: Identifies strengthening mechanisms of alloys at 20 K.
Method highlight: Evaluates the impact of twinning and ω-phase transformation.
Key finding: Twinning and ω-phase transformation enhance strength.
abstract: Abstract Plastic deformation in body-centred cubic (bcc) metals and alloys is conventionally mediated by screw dislocations. Their temperature-sensitive motion is attributed to a steep rise in strength with decreasing temperature that constricts plastic zones at crack tips, leading to a ductile-to-brittle transition 1 . Here we evaluated the mechanical properties of group IV–V bcc refractory alloys with similar electronic structures at 20 K and found that these materials instead exhibit a plateau in tensile yield strength and fracture toughness as a function of temperature, with no apparent ductile-to-brittle transition. This behaviour arises from the global activation of twinning and an ω-phase transformation, which nucleate dislocations at interfaces before global dislocation motion. The initial mechanism is temperature insensitive and controls yielding, thereby preventing a crack-tip plastic zone from constricting with decreasing temperature.

title: Physics-informed machine learning: a hybrid lens for fluid dynamics
Structural bias enables reliable sim-to-real transfer in reinforcement learning for robot swarms
summary_zh: 研究机器人群体强化学习，通过结构约束实现模拟到现实迁移。提出SwarmACB方法，评估多机器人系统性能。
summary_en: This study focuses on reinforcement learning for robot swarms, achieving reliable sim-to-real transfer through structural constraints. The SwarmACB method is introduced to evaluate performance in multi-robot systems.
insights: 创新点：结构约束在强化学习中的应用
方法亮点：SwarmACB方法提出
关键发现：提高模拟到现实迁移的可靠性
insights_en: Novelty: Application of structural constraints in reinforcement learning
Method highlight: Introduction of SwarmACB method
Key finding: Improved reliability of sim-to-real transfer
abstract: Reinforcement learning offers a powerful framework for automatically generating control policies for robot swarms, yet its application to physical multirobot systems has been limited by the simulation-to-reality gap. Despite substantial advances in multiagent reinforcement learning, systematic demonstrations of gradient-based sim-to-real transfer to physical robot swarms remain scarce. Most work remains confined to simulation, and the few real-robot demonstrations lack evaluation across multiple runs and tasks. We show that this barrier can be overcome by embedding structural constraints into policy learning. We introduce attention-based counterfactual policy gradients for behavior selection in robot swarms (SwarmACB), a multiagent actor-critic method in which robots arbitrate among predefined behavior modules—reactive sensorimotor routines such as phototaxis or aggregation—rather than learning low-level motor commands. This architectural choice reduces the variance of learned solutions, which we argue mitigates overfitting to simulation artifacts. Through systematic evaluation on five collective missions using 20 physical e-puck robots (250 real-robot runs), we demonstrate that SwarmACB transfers successfully from simulation to reality, substantially outperforming continuous-action baselines. By progressively constraining policy architecture, perception, and model capacity, we show that smaller, structured policies transfer more reliably than large, unconstrained ones. These findings challenge the assumption that scale is necessary for successful transfer, suggesting instead that principled structural design enables reinforcement learning to produce control software for robot swarms that is both learned automatically and directly deployable in the physical world.

title: Reducing energy and air consumption in scuba diving with underwater exoskeletons
summary_zh: 研究水下外骨骼辅助潜水，降低能量和空气消耗。探讨外骨骼在潜水运动中的应用。
summary_en: This study investigates the use of underwater exoskeletons to reduce energy and air consumption during scuba diving, exploring the application of exoskeletons in underwater movement.
insights: 创新点：水下外骨骼在潜水中的应用
方法亮点：能量消耗降低研究
关键发现：空气消耗减少
insights_en: Novelty: Application of underwater exoskeletons in diving
Method highlight: Reduction in energy consumption study
Key finding: Reduction in air consumption
abstract: Assisting underwater locomotion with exoskeletons could reduce energy and air consumption during scuba diving.

title: PASG-RoboKeyBench: A Closed-Loop Automated Framework and Benchmark for Operation Primitive Extraction and Semantic Anchoring in Robotic Manipulation
Tensor-space joint optimisation of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems
summary_zh: 提出三张量框架，分别编码图结构、时变信道状态和角色分配，实现拓扑角色配置的联合优化。
summary_en: A three-tensor framework is proposed to separately encode graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments for joint optimization of topology-role configuration in multi-agent systems.
insights: 创新点：提出三张量框架进行联合优化。
方法亮点：利用张量代数求解。
关键发现：拓扑角色配置的优化。
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing a three-tensor framework for joint optimization.
Method highlight: Utilizing tensor algebra for solution.
Key finding: Optimization of topology-role configuration.
abstract: Topology-role coupling is central to multi-agent formation control, yet its combinatorial complexity makes analytical treatment challenging. We propose a three-tensor framework that separately encodes graph structure, time-varying channel states, and role assignments. Their contraction yields a coupling metric equal to the mean of the non-trivial Laplacian eigenvalues, which serves as a tractable joint optimisation objective. Within this framework, the optimal leader emerges intrinsically from the tensor algebra, without recourse to heuristic rules or external designation. Optimisation is performed via spectral gradient flow restricted to a Tucker-compressed subspace, using incremental updates and warm starts from previous solutions. Under mild assumptions, Tucker compression guarantees polynomial complexity, and the gradient flow is proven to converge. Simulations demonstrate substantially better scaling than exhaustive combinatorial search as agent numbers grow. The framework unifies multi-agent control, graph theory, and tensor algebra, providing a principled foundation for scalable coordination in networked systems. Here, the authors develop a tensor-based framework for jointly optimizing communication topology and role assignment in multi-agent systems. They establish theoretical guarantees for the proposed optimization and demonstrate improved scalability and performance over combinatorial approaches.

title: Ultrafast single-qubit gates through multi-photon transition removal
summary_zh: 通过去除多光子跃迁实现超快单量子比特门，在6.8纳秒脉冲持续时间内，X和X/2门保真度超过99.98%。
summary_en: Ultrafast single-qubit gates are achieved by removing multi-photon transitions, with fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration for X and X/2 gates.
insights: 创新点：通过去除多光子跃迁实现超快单量子比特门。
方法亮点：采用衍生活动门脉冲形状去除直接跃迁。
关键发现：实现了低于2.0×10^-5的总泄漏错误。
insights_en: Novelty: Ultrafast single-qubit gates are achieved by removing multi-photon transitions.
Method highlight: Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape is used to remove direct transitions.
Key finding: Total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 is achieved.
abstract: Abstract Fast qubit control is essential for scalable quantum computing. However, the strong driving that is required can induce significant leakage from the computational subspace, particularly in weakly anharmonic qubits. We demonstrate single qubit gates with a total leakage error consistently below 2.0 × 10 −5 on a transmon qubit, and obtain fidelities above 99.98% at 6.8 ns pulse duration in both X and X /2 gates. This is achieved by removing direct transitions beyond nearest-neighbor levels using double recursive applications of Derivative Removal by Adiabatic Gate pulse shape. We also introduce the amplified leakage error sequence which can directly measure the leakage error down to 10 −6 . We test single qubit gates across a range of pulse durations using multiple benchmarking methods to reveal the error channels. The presented approach can be straightforwardly adapted by other platforms.

title: Enhancing bosonic qubit protection by squeezing
summary_zh: 通过压缩量子态增强玻色子量子比特保护，延长量子信息编码的相干时间。
summary_en: Bosonic qubit protection is enhanced by squeezing quantum states, prolonging the coherence time of quantum information encoding.
insights: 创新点：利用压缩量子态增强玻色子量子比特保护。
方法亮点：通过压缩技术减少环境测量强度。
关键发现：压缩技术延长了量子信息编码的相干时间。
insights_en: Novelty: Utilizing squeezing to enhance bosonic qubit protection.
Method highlight: Reducing the environment's measurement strength through compression techniques.
Key finding: Squeezing prolongs the coherence time of quantum information encoding.
abstract: Bosonic qubits implement error correction by harnessing the high-dimensional Hilbert space of a harmonic oscillator to redundantly encode logical quantum information. Squeezing of quantum states — a cornerstone of precision metrology — redistributes uncertainty between conjugate quadratures to enhance sensitivity in one variable at the expense of the other. In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. By redistributing uncertainty to that quadrature, squeezing can be leveraged to reduce the environment’s measurement strength, thereby prolonging coherence. Here, we exploit this insight to implement a squeezing deformation of the simplest bosonic code — the cat qubit — extending the bit-flip time with minimal impact on the phase-flip rate. We observe a dramatic reduction in bit-flip errors, achieving a 160-fold improvement over standard cat qubits and bringing multi-cat architectures closer to fault-tolerant quantum computation. In bosonic codes, decoherence can be seen as the environment performing an unwanted measurement on a noise-sensitive quadrature, collapsing superpositions and inducing errors. Here, the authors show how to use squeezing to further protect bosonic codes from noise, extending the bit-flip times of the cat qubit by two orders of magnitude without reducing phase-flip times.

title: Observation of inherent chiral Smith–Purcell effect via symmetry breaking
summary_zh: 通过对称破缺观察固有的手性Smith–Purcell效应，实现高偏振度的宽带辐射。
summary_en: The inherent chiral Smith–Purcell effect is observed via symmetry breaking, achieving broadband radiation with a high degree of polarization.
insights: 创新点：通过对称破缺观察手性Smith–Purcell效应。
方法亮点：利用非手性非谐振硅光栅。
关键发现：实现高偏振度的宽带辐射。
insights_en: Novelty: The inherent chiral Smith–Purcell effect is observed via symmetry breaking.
Method highlight: Utilizing a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating.
Key finding: Achieving broadband radiation with a high degree of polarization.
abstract: The Smith–Purcell effect arises when charged particles move near a periodic structure, emitting radiation. Conventional approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation rely on metasurface phase engineering or resonant mode interference, typically producing narrow-band, weakly chiral emission. Here, we introduce a resonance-interference-free mechanism that leverages the properties of the charged particles themselves. Using a non-chiral, non-resonant silicon grating, we demonstrate broadband, tunable Smith–Purcell radiation with high chirality, achieving a record-high degree of polarization of 0.87. This is enabled by converting the transverse spin angular momentum of electron-induced evanescent waves into a longitudinal form, producing opposite chirality at different azimuthal angles. Beam twisting or displacement offers precise control over chirality, paving the way for compact chiral light sources, advanced X-ray imaging, and integrated particle diagnostics platforms. Existing approaches for generating chiral Smith–Purcell radiation remain limited. Here, the authors overcome these limitations by uncovering the inherent chirality of the Smith–Purcell effect using non-chiral, non-resonant silicon gratings. By controlling the electron–grating configuration, this chirality can be selectively manipulated to produce tunable and highly chiral polarized radiation.

title: Chemistry-infused bandit framework for interpretable autonomous campaign of electrocatalysis
summary_zh: 本文提出一种可解释的自主电催化实验框架。结合可解释人工智能与电化学平台，实现12维空间的电催化氢析出反应自主探索。通过化学信息指导，建立化学增强的探索者，实现合成条件与电催化活性之间的局部二次近似。
summary_en: This paper proposes an interpretable autonomous framework for electrocatalysis experiments. By integrating interpretable AI with an electrochemical platform, it enables autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction. Guided by chemistry-informed hypotheses, a chemistry-infused explorer reflects the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities.
insights: 创新点：结合化学信息与人工智能实现电催化实验的自主探索
方法亮点：提出化学增强的探索者模型
关键发现：实现合成条件与电催化活性之间的局部二次近似
insights_en: Novelty: Combining chemistry information with AI for autonomous electrocatalysis experiments
Method highlight: Proposing a chemistry-infused explorer model
Key finding: Achieving locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities
abstract: Abstract Autonomous experimentation offers a time-efficient route towards accelerated catalyst discovery, but current practices often rely on black-box models that are difficult to interpret. Here we demonstrate the paradigm of interpretable autonomous exploration of a 12-dimensional space in the electrocatalytic hydrogen evolution reaction by integrating an interpretable decision-making artificial intelligence with a fully automated electrochemical platform. Guided by a human’s chemistry-informed hypothesis, a chemistry-infused bandit is established to reflect the locally quadratic approximation between synthetic conditions and electrocatalytic activities near the explored optimum region. Not only does such a decision-making bandit lead to the discovery of previously unreported, earth-abundant electrocatalysts at least comparable to Pt-based ones, the bandit also reveals model-derived hypothesis for how synthetic conditions affect the electrocatalysts’ performance near the identified local optima as autonomous inquiry proceeds, which is otherwise untenable from black-box ones. Incorporating chemistry-informed hypothesis into the decision-making bandit is generally applicable to any chemistry problem and offers a framework for autonomous investigation, advancing hypothesis generation for catalyst’s design principles beyond simple optimization.

title: Critically coupled zeroth-order resonance for ultrathin nonlinear photonics
summary_zh: 本文建立金属背腔设计规则，最大化光-物质相互作用。通过确保零阶共振与临界耦合的同时满足，推导出封闭形式的解析条件，将(n, k)平面划分为临界耦合、过耦合和欠耦合区域。
summary_en: This paper establishes a design rule for metal-backed cavities to maximize light-matter interaction. By ensuring the simultaneous satisfaction of zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling, it derives a closed-form analytical condition that partitions the (n, k) plane into critically coupled, over-coupled, and under-coupled regimes.
insights: 创新点：提出金属背腔设计规则
方法亮点：确保零阶共振与临界耦合的同时满足
关键发现：(n, k)平面划分为不同耦合区域
insights_en: Novelty: Proposing a design rule for metal-backed cavities
Method highlight: Ensuring simultaneous satisfaction of zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling
Key finding: Partitioning the (n, k) plane into different coupling regimes
abstract: Ultrathin active materials are essential for compact nonlinear and quantum photonic devices, yet no general principle exists to link their optical constants to the cavity designs required for simultaneous field buildup and reflection suppression. Consequently, achieving extreme optical confinement currently relies on trial-and-error optimization for every new material. Here, we establish a design rule for metal-backed cavities that maximizes light-matter interaction by ensuring the simultaneous satisfaction of zeroth-order resonance and critical coupling. We derive a closed-form analytical condition that partitions the (n, k) plane into critically coupled, over-coupled, and under-coupled regimes, each mapping to a specific minimal architecture. The critical curve admits a three-layer open cavity, the over-coupled region a closed cavity with a semi-transparent top mirror, and the under-coupled region a spacer-assisted geometry. For low-loss materials, the closed cavity spatially separates dissipation from field accumulation, allowing the quality factor to be controlled by the external mirror rather than intrinsic medium absorption. We validate this framework with 3R-MoS2, demonstrating a second-harmonic enhancement of 1.19 x 10^5 relative to a monolayer, accompanied by the near-complete suppression of reflected pump waves. These results provide a universal framework for efficient light-matter interaction in ultrathin nonlinear and quantum photonics.

title: Contactless continuous guidance of matter in its main states using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields
summary_zh: 研究提出使用弯曲拉长贝塞尔声场引导物质。方法上，利用声波实现非接触操控。结果显示，可引导连续物质流动。
summary_en: This study proposes guiding matter in its main states using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields. The method uses sound waves for contactless manipulation. The results show that continuous flow of matter can be guided.
insights: 创新点：提出使用弯曲拉长贝塞尔声场引导物质
方法亮点：利用声波实现非接触操控
关键发现：可引导连续物质流动
insights_en: Novelty: Proposes guiding matter using curved elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields
Method highlight: Utilizes sound waves for contactless manipulation
Key finding: Continuous flow of matter can be guided
abstract: Acoustic manipulation uses sound waves to exert force on matter, enabling contactless movement, trapping, and the structuring of particles in bulk media. It offers a contamination-free approach for handling matter in applications spanning across chemistry, biology, and advanced manufacturing. However, state-of-the-art techniques, including acoustic holograms or phased arrays of transducers (PATs) are limited to transporting individual particles or small clusters one by one, and are not suitable for dispersed matter such as gases or aerosols. Here, we introduce a method for guiding a continuous flow of matter along reconfigurable three-dimensional trajectories using elongated Bessel-like acoustic fields (EBAFs). These fields generate converging radial acoustic forces along a programmable path, forming stable mid-air conduits that continuously transport matter. Compared to existing methods such as near-field acoustic levitation, acoustofluidic separation, particle manipulation with vortex and Airy beams, the proposed method offers enhanced versatility, scalability, and real-time control of transport trajectories in mid-air without requiring physical guiding structures. We developed methods to generate EBAFs with PATs tailored to different particle sizes and material properties, and experimentally demonstrated guidance of solids, liquids, aerosols, and gases along programmable trajectories. This technique enables containerless laboratory operations, precise and contamination-free reagent or energy delivery, and integration into advanced additive manufacturing processes that require controlled distribution of matter in different states to target zones.
